title: Choose Tailor's new look
question: Four complete directions for the new Tailor. Every one is bright by default, has a matching dark mode, keeps the 3D resume and fluid background on the landing, and carries into Review and Results. Pick one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: Precision Instrument
options.lineage: calibrated lab meters and measuring stages
options.thesis: Tailor as an honest measuring instrument: your resume is the sample, the match rate is a calibrated reading.
options.viewport: Left: headline and the two actions. Right: the 3D resume lies on a lit measuring stage; a scan line sweeps it, a bullet rewrites, matched keywords tick on and the needle climbs into the green target band. Behind: a slow flowing iso-line field like a calibration pattern.
options.risk: Can feel clinical for a stressed job seeker; the metaphor is strongest for the score and needs care on the rewriting screens.

raised.raise: Depth as layers moving at different speeds: field, faceplate and resume sample parallax as three planes, which carries the depth on Review and Results.
Total palette commitment: two inks (graphite on white enamel) and one signal colour, nothing else.
Evidence strength drawn as line weight: exact matches heavy, similar-wording matches light, on the report and Review.
Scale follows importance: required keywords and the score set larger, everything else steps down.
One light source: the tailored resume is the brightest object on every screen.

options.label: Editor's Proof
options.lineage: copy editors' proof sheets and margin marks
options.thesis: Every change shown the way an editor marks a proof: struck, inserted, explained in the margin, and yours to keep or reverse.
options.viewport: A printed proof of a sample resume on the desk in 3D, tilting with the cursor; proof marks draw themselves: a caret inserts a keyword, a stroke removes a filler word, a margin note says why. Blue ink diffuses slowly behind it.
options.risk: Familiar: editorial looks are where many runs in this category land, and red marks can read as criticism of the user's writing.

options.label: Highlighter Explainer
options.thesis: Tailor explains itself like a friend with highlighters: swipes mark matched keywords, arrows run from your words to the rewrite.
options.viewport: Marker headline with a highlighter swipe; the 3D resume with yellow swipes landing on keywords and a drawn arrow to the improved bullet; numbered steps sketched below.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: highlighters are how people already match a job ad to a resume; wins on clarity, loses on audience identification (too playful for senior candidates and for the calm, no-hype voice).
options.risk: Can read as a toy; mascots and doodles undercut trust at a stressful moment.

options.label: Azulejo Hall
options.thesis: Cobalt on milk-white tiles, panels framed by borders.
options.viewport: A tiled hall with the resume painted across the grid.
options.case: Fuses poorly: job seekers do not identify with heritage tilework, and ornament competes with the text being compared.

options.label: Multiplane Dawn
options.thesis: Painted planes sliding at different speeds.
options.viewport: The resume on the nearest plane, forest behind.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a storybook forest says nothing about resumes or job applications.
options.kept: Depth as planes moving at different speeds.

options.label: Event Display
options.case: Fuses poorly, and it is dark-first, which the owner ruled out.

options.label: Mezzotint Night
options.thesis: Images burnished out of velvet black.
options.case: Fuses poorly: black-first, the opposite of the brief.
options.kept: One light source: the result is the brightest thing.

options.label: Telop Captions
options.viewport: Keywords pop as captions over the resume.
options.case: Fuses poorly: loud and comic against a calm, trustworthy voice.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean modern resume tool, executed impeccably: white, one blue accent, rounded cards, soft shadows.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and actions on the left, the 3D resume floating on the right over a soft blue gradient field.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other resume tool by design.
